verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 12.22
verses.english: Linked Discourses 12.22

verses.pali: 3. Dasabalavagga
verses.english: 3. The Ten Powers

verses.pali: Dutiyadasabalasutta
verses.english: The Ten Powers (2nd)

verses.pali: Sāvatthiyaṁ viharati.
verses.english: At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “Dasabalasamannāgato, bhikkhave, tathāgato catūhi ca vesārajjehi samannāgato āsabhaṁ ṭhānaṁ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṁ nadati, brahmacakkaṁ pavatteti:
verses.english: “Mendicants, a Realized One has ten powers and four kinds of self-assurance. With these he claims the bull’s place, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and turns the divine wheel.

verses.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the ending of feeling.

verses.pali: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the ending of perception.

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo,
verses.english: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the ending of choices.

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.

verses.pali: Iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
verses.english: When this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

verses.pali: imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati.
verses.english: When this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:

verses.pali: Yadidaṁ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā;
verses.english: Ignorance is a requirement for choices.

verses.pali: saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṁ …pe…
verses.english: Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …

verses.pali: evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti.
verses.english: That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

verses.pali: Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho;
verses.english: When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.

verses.pali: saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho …pe…
verses.english: When choices cease, consciousness ceases. …

verses.pali: evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti’.
verses.english: That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

verses.pali: Evaṁ svākkhāto, bhikkhave, mayā dhammo uttāno vivaṭo pakāsito chinnapilotiko.
verses.english: The teaching well-explained thus by me is clarified, revealed, illuminated, and stripped of patchwork.

verses.pali: Evaṁ svākkhāte kho, bhikkhave, mayā dhamme uttāne vivaṭe pakāsite chinnapilotike alameva saddhāpabbajitena kulaputtena vīriyaṁ ārabhituṁ:
verses.english: In this teaching thus well-explained, it is quite enough for a gentleman who has gone forth out of faith to rouse up energy.

verses.pali: ‘kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu, sarīre upassussatu maṁsalohitaṁ. Yaṁ taṁ purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena pattabbaṁ, na taṁ apāpuṇitvā vīriyassa saṇṭhānaṁ bhavissatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Gladly, let only skin, sinews, and tendons remain! Let the flesh and blood waste away in my body! I will not stop trying until I have achieved what is possible by human strength, energy, and vigor.’

verses.pali: Dukkhaṁ, bhikkhave, kusīto viharati vokiṇṇo pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi, mahantañca sadatthaṁ parihāpeti.
verses.english: A lazy person lives in suffering, mixed up with bad, unskillful qualities, neglecting their heart’s great goal.

verses.pali: Āraddhavīriyo ca kho, bhikkhave, sukhaṁ viharati pavivitto pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi, mahantañca sadatthaṁ paripūreti.
verses.english: But an energetic person lives happily, secluded from bad, unskillful qualities, fulfilling their heart’s great goal.

verses.pali: Na, bhikkhave, hīnena aggassa patti hoti.
verses.english: The best isn’t reached by the worst.

verses.pali: Aggena ca kho, bhikkhave, aggassa patti hoti.
verses.english: The best is reached by the best.

verses.pali: Maṇḍapeyyamidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ, satthā sammukhībhūto.
verses.english: This spiritual life is the cream, mendicants, and the Teacher is before you.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, vīriyaṁ ārabhatha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
verses.english: So you should rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘Evaṁ no ayaṁ amhākaṁ pabbajjā avañjhā bhavissati saphalā saudrayā.
verses.english: ‘In this way our going forth will not be barren, but will be fruitful and fertile.

verses.pali: Yesañca mayaṁ paribhuñjāma cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ tesaṁ te kārā amhesu mahapphalā bhavissanti mahānisaṁsā’ti—
verses.english: And the services of those whose robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick we enjoy shall be very fruitful and beneficial for them.’

verses.pali: evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṁ.
verses.english: That’s how you should train.

verses.pali: Attatthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetuṁ;
verses.english: Considering what is good for yourself, mendicants, is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.

verses.pali: paratthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetuṁ;
verses.english: Considering what is good for others is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.

verses.pali: ubhayatthaṁ vā hi, bhikkhave, sampassamānena alameva appamādena sampādetun”ti.
verses.english: Considering what is good for both is quite enough for you to persist with diligence.”

verses.pali: Dutiyaṁ.
